_note: Add items at the top. 'date' is YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Items below were seeded from the PubMed record; add awards, arrivals, talks, and funding.

items.title: Plasma cell-free metagenomic sequencing predicts bloodstream infection
items.text: A prospective study with collaborators at St. Jude, published in The Lancet Microbe, evaluates plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing for predicting bloodstream infection in children with cancer.

items.title: Bill Evans becomes CEO of BioSkryb Genomics
items.text: William E. Evans, former President and CEO of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and a long-time collaborator of the lab, becomes Chief Executive Officer of BioSkryb Genomics, the company founded to bring PTA to researchers and clinics.

items.title: Somatic mitochondrial DNA mutations shape cellular heterogeneity
items.text: Work led with the Kundu lab, published in Science Advances, shows that intermediate-heteroplasmy mtDNA mutations are a source of functional heterogeneity among primary cells.

items.title: Longitudinal single-cell clonal evolution of pediatric ALL
items.text: A preprint from the lab measures genome-wide clonal evolution in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia across diagnosis, treatment, and relapse at single-cell resolution.

items.title: Single-cell multiomics scales to thousands of cells per run
items.text: A 384-well ResolveOME workflow with Tecan's Uno Single Cell Dispenser, and a collaboration with Ultima Genomics, bring paired genome and transcriptome sequencing to thousands of cells per experiment.

items.title: 1Cell.Ai and BioSkryb to co-develop single-cell multiomic solutions
items.text: 1Cell.Ai joins forces with BioSkryb Genomics, the company founded to commercialize PTA, to co-develop and commercialize next-generation single-cell multiomic products.

items.title: Residual leukemia cells, sequenced one at a time, offered as a service
items.text: ResolveSEQ MRD pairs flow-sorted measurable residual disease cells with single-cell genome and transcriptome sequencing to ask why some cells survive therapy, an approach that grew out of this lab's work on persistent leukemia cells.

items.title: Cellular phenotype dynamics in Nature Genetics
items.text: A collaboration with the Landau lab defines heritability, plasticity, and transition dynamics of cellular phenotypes using single-cell multi-omics.

items.title: PTA-based single-cell technology joins the Human Cell Atlas
items.text: BioSkryb Genomics partners with the Human Cell Atlas to broaden access to single-cell genome and transcriptome sequencing for atlas-building projects.

items.title: scMicrobe PTA: near-complete genomes from single bacterial cells
items.text: With the DOE Joint Genome Institute, the lab shows that PTA recovers near-complete genomes from individual bacterial cells, published in ISME Communications.

items.title: Whole genome and transcriptome core kits released
items.text: BioSkryb releases ResolveDNA and ResolveOME core kits, making PTA-based single-cell whole genome and paired genome-plus-transcriptome amplification available as standard reagents.

items.title: Genome plus transcriptome from the same single cell goes commercial
items.text: The paired single-cell genome and full-length transcriptome method developed with PTA launches commercially as ResolveOME, together with the BaseJumper analysis platform, at the AGBT meeting.

items.title: PTA licensed for preimplantation genetic testing
items.text: CooperSurgical's genomics division signs a multi-year exclusive license to BioSkryb's PTA chemistry for preimplantation genetic testing and women's reproductive health worldwide.

items.title: PTA published in PNAS
items.text: Primary template-directed amplification, the lab's method for accurate single-cell genome amplification, is published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
